summary: In Genesis, מַבּוּל names the flood whose rising waters lifted Noah’s ark. Psalm 29 speaks of Yahweh enthroned over the flood.

senses.definition: An inundation in which rising waters cover the land.

evidence.note: In מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, “the waters of the flood,” הַמַּבּוּל identifies the flood whose waters drove Noah and his family into the ark.
The flood lasts forty days, and its rising waters lift the ark above the earth.
Yahweh sits enthroned over the flood and reigns forever.
God announces to Noah that he will bring a flood of water upon the earth.
After seven days מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, “the waters of the flood,” were upon the earth.
Sons were born to Shem, Ham, and Japheth אַחַר הַמַּבּוּל, “after the flood.”
The verse describes הַמַּבּוּל as מַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ, “water upon the earth.”

In מִמֵּי הַמַּבּוּל, “by the waters of the flood,” the article identifies the flood Noah survived. God promises that its waters will never again cut off all flesh. The next clause repeats מַבּוּל without the article in the promise that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.
God promises that הַמַּיִם, “the waters,” will never again become a flood (לְמַבּוּל). The following phrase לְשַׁחֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר, “to destroy all flesh,” describes what such a flood would do.
